why: C55 cleared 331 rows by fixing the ONE lossy marker the differential deliberately does not skip. That prompted the mirror question: for the markers it DOES skip, are the excluded branches the ones that would have matched?
the_asymmetry_that_makes_this_possible: engine_transition_differential.py:1396 skips any branch carrying a lossy marker other than the Sleep Talk one. A skipped branch cannot match, so if the matching branch is skipped the boundary is reported divergent on the strength of the branches that remain.
headline: 90 of 366 (24.6%) of the remaining residue has an excluded branch that reproduces the observation
the_limit_of_this_measurement: 'Reproduces the observation' here means net HP on both slots, exactly or within the legal roll window. The matcher compares component decompositions, so a branch can agree on HP and still be rejected. 90 is a CANDIDATE population, not a predicted delta. Recording that explicitly because the same HP-level test under-predicted C55 by 4x -- it can err in either direction.
what_this_does_NOT_license: Simply un-skipping these branches. The markers exist because the render is genuinely ambiguous -- an Attract tail with no attributable owner, a confusion expiry that is not observable. Admitting an ambiguous branch to the comparison could manufacture false MATCHES, which is worse than a false divergence because it hides a real difference. C55 was safe precisely because it ADDED a description of damage that demonstrably happened; this would REMOVE a guard. The two are not the same move and I am not going to treat them as one.
next: take the largest marker, attract_empty_tail_ambiguous at 123 branches, and ask the C55 question rather than the un-skip question: is the render ambiguous because information is genuinely unavailable, or because the renderer declines to emit something it could compute? C55 turned out to be the second.
does_not_reach_a_pass: no code changed; unattributed stays at 366
